findings.title: Security disable is reported as "not implemented"
findings.body: ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression with fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). That message is false: SQL expressions were implemented and are being turned off because of CVE-2024-9264. enableSqlExpressions (line 194) also reads FlagSqlExpressions with inverted polarity and then returns false on both branches, so enabling the documented feature flag does not change the result and is not mentioned in the error. Clients and operators will treat a security kill-switch as a missing feature or a malformed query, and anyone following the feature-flag docs will not be able to tell why SQL expressions stopped working. Return a stable error that states SQL expressions are disabled for security, and do not consult the flag unless it can actually enable a safe path.

findings.title: Legacy SQL path fails as bad SQL and logs every query
findings.body: The pipeline that still builds commands through UnmarshalSQLCommand does not use the new reader kill-switch. NewSQLCommand always calls sql.TablesList, which now always errors because the stub DB refuses RunCommands. That expected failure is logged at Warn with the full user SQL (line 32) and again at Error in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:28 (including the constructed statement), then returned as BadRequest with public message "error reading SQL command" (line 34). Alert evaluations and panel refreshes that still contain a SQL expression will therefore emit error-level logs of the raw query on every tick and show a message that blames the SQL text. That hides the security disable, floods logs, and can copy sensitive literals from expressions into error logs. Reject in NewSQLCommand/Execute with an explicit disabled error before TablesList, and do not log the query at Error for this intentional failure.

findings.title: User SQL is still interpolated into a DuckDB statement
findings.body: TablesList still quote-doubles apostrophes and builds SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s') from the raw user query, then passes that string to RunCommands. Apostrophe doubling is not a safe DuckDB string sanitizer (other quote forms and escapes can break out). This is the same sink class as CVE-2024-9264, and it is reached from UnmarshalSQLCommand, which never calls enableSqlExpressions. The reader comment says ExpressionQueryReader has not replaced the existing Query path in transform.go, so the historical request path is this one. Execution is stopped only because pkg/expr/sql/db.go RunCommands and QueryFramesInto return "not implemented"; Execute in sql_command.go:100 still forwards the raw user query into QueryFramesInto. Filling in those stubs, or any caller that ignores the error, reactivates injection and RCE without passing the reader gate. Delete the statement construction and fail closed before any command string is built.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions cannot execute
findings.body: This is the in-tree fix for critical CVE-2024-9264 (DuckDB SQL expressions allowing remote code execution and local file read), but no test was added or updated. Nothing asserts that a SQL expression is rejected, that FlagSqlExpressions cannot turn it back on, or that a file-read or command-execution statement passed through NewSQLCommand, TablesList, or Execute does not succeed. Disablement is split between an always-false helper and stub methods whose errors say "not implemented", so a later cleanup can restore execution without a failing test. Add a unit test that malicious SQL is rejected and that RunCommands/QueryFramesInto cannot execute it.
